info.name: Gateway fault flows (LLM OpenAI-compatible errors)
info.description: Exercises the policy-engine fault flow with `[policy_engine.llm_errors] disable_openai_format = false` against a mock LLM backend (`mock-backend.py`). See README.md in this folder.

variable.description: The mock backend as the gateway runtime reaches it (compose service name).

item.name: 7. SDK FaultDetails and fault-policy priority

request.description: sample-sdk-fault returns ImmediateResponse{Fault: FaultDetails{...}} with no body.

exec: pm.test("status is 401 (the formatter never changes it)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

pm.test("error.message is Invalid API key", () => pm.expect(body.error.message).to.eql("Invalid API key"));
pm.test("no Envoy internals leak into the message", () => pm.expect(body.error.message.toLowerCase()).to.not.include("upstream connect error"));

pm.test("no fault policy on this route", () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("x-sample-fault-handler")).to.be.undefined);

item.description: sample-sdk-fault describes its failure in FaultDetails (the SDK way); sample-fault-handler is a fault policy that stamps x-sample-fault-handler with what it saw and can re-describe, write a body, or change the status. Priority: fault-policy body > fault-policy re-description > producer FaultDetails > producer body (a fallback). Backend errors pass through unless a fault policy writes a body.
